searchText: A question about EIP-7702: why do we have the chainID in each authorization? we only accept authorizations for the current chain anyway, and the chainID is contained in the transacction already I understand that it's an input into the signature, but we could technically get it from the transaction It would save a few bytes not to have this redundant information in each auth almost feel bad for bringing this up, since we're so close to the finish line with 7702 but would be nice to investigate if it's possible to remove this field, especially since we are considering to expand it to uint256 right now ahh, I see that EIP-7702 also permits a `chain_id` of zero we could keep that case working by creating a boolean field that signals compatibility with all chains or combine with signature `v` I recommend against bit packing. While it does save some bytes, the pain and suffering it causes for developers forever is quite high. yeah it's OK I wasn't entirely serious about putting it into `v` We saw this when chain ID was added to transactions with EIP-155, which resulted in many bugs and countless wasted hours. just want to see how small we can make it honestly RLP encoded number 0 is 1 byte I think? yes Or is this SSZ encoded? no it's not SSZ could've been, but we're not opening that back up right now published the above idea as a proposal here: https://github.com/ethereum/EIPs/pull/9152 btw, in practice, this proposal will not save any bytes on mainnet the `chain_id` is one there, and under the new proposal the first element of the auth tuple is always one byte also https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/issues/4064 - on block and transaction sizes - el devs are in particular invited to provide feedback on approach (b) - (d) has its advantages but is pretty tricky to get right on the CL side 256 bits on SSZ
